drift.client_visible_effect: New 504 {"error":"Request timeout"} + X-Gateway-Error: backend_timeout when a Gateway API HTTPRoute timeouts.request / mesh_route_dispatch request_timeout_ms budget expires (including BEFORE dispatch or in retry backoff, error_class dispatch_policy_rejected). timeouts.backendRequest / attempt_timeout_ms cut a streaming body (HTTP/2 reset, HTTP/1.1 close). drift.anvil_impact: Redis-outage fixtures behave differently between versions; 429 boundary timing tests must be version-scoped.

outcomes.condition: reqwest (HTTP/1.1) lane: DestinationRule connectionPool.tcp.maxConnections reached for the destination; no socket opened.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to open another connection to this upstream because a gateway-configured connection ceiling is reached; the request was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is down or returned 503 (despite backend_error).
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review maxConnections for this destination.
outcomes.notes: Same condition on direct-H2/H3/gRPC pools surfaces as 502 'Backend unavailable' + connection_failure (upstream.connection_limit.pooled). WebSocket upgrade path uses the same 503 body (mod.rs:14769).

outcomes.condition: DestinationRule connectionPool.http.http1MaxPendingRequests reached for the backend (upstream overflow) on the reqwest lane.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge shed this request because a gateway-configured in-flight request limit for the upstream is reached; the request was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned 503 or is unhealthy.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff; gateway operator: review http1MaxPendingRequests.
outcomes.notes: Carries backend_error although no backend was contacted.

outcomes.condition: Literal-IP backend (or dns_override) blocked by the backend egress policy; no dial.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to contact the configured backend address because gateway egress policy blocks it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned an error or is down.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: fix the backend address or egress allow/deny policy.
outcomes.notes: H3 cross-protocol bridge additionally sets gateway-error-reason: backend-egress-policy-denied (src/http3/cross_protocol.rs:1618).

outcomes.condition: reqwest dispatch where proxy dns_override conflicts with a literal-IP backend URL host.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"backend DNS override cannot be applied to literal target"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the route's DNS override cannot be applied to the configured literal backend address (gateway configuration issue).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: correct the route's dns_override/backend host.

outcomes.condition: Backend TLS SNI override that neither the direct-H2 pool nor the reqwest dial can honor.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the route's backend TLS server-name override cannot be honored on this path (gateway configuration issue).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend certificate is wrong or the backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: review the BackendTLSPolicy/SNI override and backend protocol.
outcomes.notes: gateway-error-reason is an undocumented gateway-authored response header; it is NOT stripped from backend responses, so it is spoofable.

outcomes.condition: Mesh-only: target requires HBONE / sidecar mTLS / Unix-socket transport that is unavailable for this attempt.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Bad Gateway","message":"Mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target"} | {"error":"Bad Gateway","message":"Unix socket retry dispatch unavailable"}
public_signal.transport: complete HTTP response; gRPC trailers-only UNAVAILABLE

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the secured mesh transport required for this backend was unavailable.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend application failed.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway/mesh operator: check gateway mesh identity and transport availability.
outcomes.notes: Mesh deployments only; included for completeness. Reason strings include 'mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target', 'Unix socket retry dispatch is unavailable', 'HBONE transport or gateway identity is unavailable for retry target'.

outcomes.condition: Backend returned a complete 5xx response other than 504 (connection_error=false).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The response was relayed by Ferrum Edge with a 5xx status that, per the gateway's coarse marker, came from or after the upstream exchange; the marker alone does not prove the backend application authored it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway failed, or (without body/provenance evidence) that the application itself produced it: several gateway-local refusals also carry backend_error.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: inspect backend logs for this request; compare body with known gateway bodies.
outcomes.notes: Backend-supplied X-Gateway-Error values are stripped and replaced on this path (mod.rs:39449).

outcomes.condition: Backend itself returned a complete 504 response (e.g. an upstream load balancer timeout).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A 504 was relayed through Ferrum Edge and marked backend_timeout; the marker is also applied when the backend itself answered 504, so only the body distinguishes it from the gateway's own timeout.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway timed out (unless the body is exactly {"error":"Backend timeout"} from a trusted Ferrum destination).
outcomes.remediation: API owner/infra behind the gateway: check the backend's own upstream timeouts.
outcomes.notes: http_observability_error_class keys backend_timeout on status 504 alone, not on ErrorClass.

outcomes.condition: Backend returned 1xx-4xx (including its own 401/403/404/429).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The upstream application's response was relayed; no gateway failure marker is present.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That a 401/403/404/429 came from the gateway (gateway plugin rejections use the same statuses).
outcomes.remediation: Treat as application result unless other provenance says otherwise.
outcomes.notes: Any X-Gateway-Error the backend sets is stripped on H1/H2/H3 backend-response paths.

outcomes.condition: All targets in the upstream (or selected subset) were unhealthy; the load balancer used the all-unhealthy / parent-upstream fallback. Any final status.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports it routed this request in degraded mode because no upstream target was considered healthy; the request itself may still have succeeded.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request failed, or which target was used.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator/API owner: investigate health-check failures for the upstream.
outcomes.notes: Spoofing: on the H1/H2 builder path a backend-supplied X-Gateway-Upstream-Status is NOT stripped when the gateway did not use fallback, and when it did, the builder appends a second field line. H3 replaces it only when is_fallback. Treat as spoofable.

outcomes.condition: Data-plane mode: last applied CP snapshot older than FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_MAX_STALE_SECONDS (default 3600) with CP authority lost and FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_STALE_ACTION=fail_closed (default).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 14 grpc-message 'Gateway configuration stale' WITHOUT X-Gateway-Error. TCP/UDP listeners: accepted socket dropped / datagram session refused (no payload).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused new work because its data plane has not received a fresh configuration from its control plane within the allowed window; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the client payload, credentials, or the backend are at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: restore control-plane connectivity / config sync; client can retry later (not dispatched).
outcomes.notes: Runs before routing, plugins and overload admission. Already-accepted connections drain. Readiness also degrades (/health ready:false).

outcomes.condition: Overload manager critical request pressure (FERRUM_MAX_REQUESTS with FERRUM_OVERLOAD_REQ_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD default 0.95) OR shutdown drain started (SIGTERM).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 14 'Service overloaded' without X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to admit this request because the gateway process is shedding load or is draining for shutdown; no upstream was contacted for this request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is unhealthy, that it is CPU overload specifically, or which of overload vs shutdown drain applied.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff (safe: request was not dispatched); gateway operator should check overload manager pressure and deployment/shutdown activity.
outcomes.notes: Drain and overload produce byte-identical responses; drain/pressure additionally add 'connection: close' to other responses (mod.rs:39490-39510). FERRUM_MAX_REQUESTS defaults to 0 (request-based shedding off).

outcomes.condition: Critical connection pressure (reject_new_connections) or the listener connection semaphore (FERRUM_MAX_CONNECTIONS, default 100000) exhausted; for TCP listeners also the stale-config fence.

public_signal.transport: accepted TCP socket dropped immediately before TLS/HTTP (code comment says 'TCP RST'; kernel may emit FIN or RST)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The connection to the gateway endpoint was closed before any TLS or HTTP response; this is consistent with gateway connection admission (overload, connection limit, stale config for L4) but also with any network middlebox or a non-listening service.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That Ferrum refused it (no Ferrum marker is possible here), or any HTTP status.
outcomes.remediation: Retry with backoff; compare with a direct health check; gateway operator can check reject/connection-limit counters.
outcomes.notes: No HTTP response possible. H3 equivalent: QUIC Incoming.refuse() (src/http3/server.rs:1146).

outcomes.condition: Circuit breaker for the proxy/target is open (or half-open probe slot taken).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: normalized to trailers-only grpc-status 14 (503->UNAVAILABLE) with grpc-message 'Service temporarily unavailable (circuit breaker open)'; x-gateway-error header is restored into the reject header map so it is expected on gRPC too (not lab-verified).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected this attempt at its circuit breaker because recent failures to this upstream exceeded the configured threshold; this attempt was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That no earlier retry attempt in the same request reached a backend, or that the backend is still failing now.
outcomes.remediation: Wait for the breaker cooldown and retry; API owner/gateway operator: investigate the upstream's recent failures.
outcomes.notes: Runs through after_proxy reject hooks (headers may be decorated) then the token is restored authoritatively. rejection_phase=circuit_breaker_open in logs.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_IP (default 0 = off) exceeded for the resolved client IP.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Too many concurrent requests from this IP"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge limited this request because too many requests from the same client IP were in flight at once.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That an API rate-limit quota (rate_limiting plugin) was exhausted.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce concurrency from this IP; no Retry-After is provided.
outcomes.notes: Pre-routing; no plugins run; no Retry-After / rate-limit headers; gRPC not specially mapped here (plain JSON).

outcomes.condition: Connection authenticated with a client certificate whose trust decision was withdrawn by an accepted client-CA/CRL reload (issue #3857).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 16 'Client certificate trust withdrawn'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge no longer trusts the client certificate this connection was established with; new requests on it are refused.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API credential/token is wrong.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reconnect with a currently trusted client certificate; operator: check client CA/CRL changes.

outcomes.condition: Request carries Early-Data: 1 (added by a trusted CDN per RFC 8470) and its method is not in the configured early-data method list.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 14

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to process this request as TLS 0-RTT early data; resend it after the handshake completes.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the method is unsupported by the API.
outcomes.remediation: Caller/CDN: retry without early data.

outcomes.condition: No proxy route matched the request host/path.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 12 grpc-message 'Not Found'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The endpoint answered 404 with Ferrum's route-miss body shape; if the destination is a trusted Ferrum gateway this means no gateway route matched this host/path.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That every 404 is a gateway route miss (backends can return the same bytes), or that the resource does not exist in the API.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check host, path prefix and scheme against the published API; gateway operator: check route configuration.
outcomes.notes: Pre-plugin: no auth/CORS plugins run, so a browser CORS failure may mask it. No Via header on this gateway-built response.

outcomes.condition: Route matched but the method is not in the route's allowed_methods.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 12

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The route exists but does not accept this HTTP method; the Allow header lists the accepted methods.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That authentication failed or the resource is missing.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: use one of the methods in Allow.
outcomes.notes: rejection_phase=allowed_methods (logs only). Allow is gateway-authoritative (policy cannot alter it).

outcomes.condition: TRACE request, or CONNECT that is not a WebSocket extended CONNECT (and not HBONE).

other_headers.Allow: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"TRACE method is not allowed"} | {"error":"CONNECT method is not allowed"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge blocks this HTTP method at the protocol level for all routes.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the route does not exist.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: do not use TRACE/CONNECT through the gateway.

outcomes.condition: Request with application/grpc content-type using a method other than POST.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only gRPC response (400 mapped to INVALID_ARGUMENT)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the gRPC call because gRPC requires POST.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the service/method does not exist.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send gRPC calls with POST.
outcomes.notes: Logged/metric status is 400.

outcomes.condition: One request header (name+value bytes) exceeds FERRUM_MAX_SINGLE_HEADER_SIZE_BYTES (default 16384).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request header '<name>' exceeds maximum size of <limit> bytes"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because one header is larger than the gateway allows; the body names the header.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: shrink the named header (often cookies or tokens).
outcomes.notes: Header name echoed (JSON-escaped). H1 parser buffer floor is 8 KiB above which hyper itself may reject first (see frontend_parse.hyper_default_rejects).

outcomes.condition: Sum of request header bytes exceeds FERRUM_MAX_HEADER_SIZE_BYTES (default 32768).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its headers are larger in total than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce header size.
outcomes.notes: On HTTP/1 a head larger than the hyper parser buffer (max(limit, 8 KiB)) is rejected by hyper before this check with hyper's own response.

outcomes.condition: Number of header fields exceeds FERRUM_MAX_HEADER_COUNT (default 100).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because it has more header fields than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send fewer headers.

outcomes.condition: path+query length exceeds FERRUM_MAX_URL_LENGTH_BYTES (default 8192).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request URL length (<n> bytes) exceeds maximum of <limit> bytes"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its URL is longer than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the resource is missing.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: shorten the URL / move data into the body.

outcomes.condition: Query parameter count exceeds FERRUM_MAX_QUERY_PARAMS (default 100).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because it has more query parameters than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected a parameter value.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send fewer query parameters.

outcomes.condition: Request body exceeds the effective limit (FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES default 10485760, FERRUM_MAX_GRPC_RECV_SIZE_BYTES default 4194304 for gRPC, or a lower route/request_size_limiting limit) while buffering or by Content-Length.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 8 'Request body exceeds maximum size of <limit> bytes'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its body exceeds the gateway's size limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend received the full body (for streamed uploads the backend may have received a truncated prefix).
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce the payload or use a chunked/multipart upload API; operator may review the limit.
outcomes.notes: The request_size_limiting plugin uses a different body shape ({"error":...,"limit":N}); see plugin outcomes. For streamed uploads exceeding the limit mid-stream the backend receives a truncated upload; client-visible shape depends on path (not fully audited).

outcomes.condition: Client upload stalled beyond the request body read timeout while the gateway was buffering it.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 4 'Request body read timed out'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge stopped waiting for the rest of the request body from the client; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend timed out.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check local upload throughput / proxy; operator: review request body timeout.

outcomes.condition: Client disconnected/aborted while the gateway was buffering its request body.

public_signal.transport: normally never observed by the client (it already disconnected)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The client side ended the upload before the gateway received the full request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway or backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check local cancellation/network.
outcomes.notes: 499 is a gateway-internal status recorded in logs/metrics.

outcomes.condition: Request smuggling / desync checks on headers: HTTP/1.0 with Transfer-Encoding, both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, invalid/non-numeric/overflowing/conflicting Content-Length, H2/H3 with Transfer-Encoding, invalid TE, missing/duplicate/invalid Host on HTTP/1.1.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request contains both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers"} | {"error":"HTTP/1.0 does not support Transfer-Encoding"} | {"error":"Content-Length header contains invalid empty value"} | {"error":"Content-Length header contains invalid non-numeric value"} | {"error":"Content-Length header exceeds supported integer range"} | {"error":"Multiple Content-Length headers with conflicting values"} | {"error":"Request contains multiple Host headers"} | {"error":"HTTP/1.1 request is missing a Host header"} | {"error":"Host header contains invalid empty value"} | {"error":"Host header contains invalid characters"} | {"error":"HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 do not support Transfer-Encoding"} | {"error":"TE header contains invalid empty value"} | {"error":"TE header must be 'trailers' or absent"} | {"error":"TE header contains invalid characters"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed or ambiguous at the HTTP protocol layer before routing; the body names the rule.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected the payload or that authentication failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the request framing/Host/path encoding shown in the body (often a client or intermediate proxy bug).
outcomes.notes: No X-Gateway-Error on protocol 400s (issue #4543).

outcomes.condition: Host header and :authority disagree, are invalid, missing, or malformed.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Host header contains invalid authority"} | {"error":"Request authority contains invalid authority"} | {"error":"Host header and request authority disagree"} | {"error":"Request contains multiple Host headers"} | {"error":"Request is missing both :authority and Host"} | {"error":"Host header contains invalid characters"} | {"error":"Request contains malformed Host or authority"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed or ambiguous at the HTTP protocol layer before routing; the body names the rule.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected the payload or that authentication failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the request framing/Host/path encoding shown in the body (often a client or intermediate proxy bug).
outcomes.notes: No X-Gateway-Error on protocol 400s (issue #4543).

outcomes.condition: Request path contains an ambiguous percent-encoding the canonical policy path refuses (GHSA-69xf-42xm-4w4f): incomplete/double-encoded escapes, encoded '/' or '\\', literal backslash, encoded control chars, (encoded) dot segments.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request path contains an incomplete percent-escape"} | {"error":"Request path contains a double-encoded percent-escape"} | {"error":"Request path contains an encoded path separator"} | {"error":"Request path contains an encoded backslash"} | {"error":"Request path contains a backslash"} | {"error":"Request path contains an encoded control character"} | {"error":"Request path contains an unrepresentable percent-escape"} | {"error":"Request path contains an encoded dot segment"} | {"error":"Request path contains a dot segment"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed or ambiguous at the HTTP protocol layer before routing; the body names the rule.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected the payload or that authentication failed.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the request framing/Host/path encoding shown in the body (often a client or intermediate proxy bug).
outcomes.notes: No X-Gateway-Error on protocol 400s (issue #4543). gRPC / gRPC-Web get grpc-status 3 with messages like 'Encoded path separator in request path' (src/policy_path.rs:228).

outcomes.condition: First HTTP/1 head on a connection has conflicting Content-Length values, HTTP/1.0+Transfer-Encoding, or an invalid UTF-8 request-target; written directly to the socket before hyper sees the request.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Multiple Content-Length headers with conflicting values"} | {"error":"HTTP/1.0 does not support Transfer-Encoding"} | {"error":"Malformed HTTP request"}
public_signal.transport: raw 'HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request' envelope then connection close

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request as malformed HTTP/1 framing before any routing and closed the connection.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend saw the request.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the client's HTTP/1 framing.
outcomes.notes: Only for the connection's first head before any response byte; later malformed heads get hyper's empty-bodied 400 (docs/error_classification.md:224-272). Before any RequestContext: no plugins/logs rows, no X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: The inbound HTTP/1 framing observer could not verify framing (state unknown/overflowed).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"HTTP/1 request framing could not be verified; connection will be closed"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge could not verify this HTTP/1 connection's request framing and closed it defensively.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request content was invalid.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: retry on a fresh connection; report if persistent.

outcomes.condition: Other malformed HTTP/1 heads hyper rejects at parse time (truncated head, non-numeric Content-Length hyper refuses, oversized head beyond the parser buffer, later heads on a pipelined connection).

public_signal.body_shape: empty body (hyper automatic response; 431 possible for an oversized head — hyper behaviour, not Ferrum code)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server rejected the request as unparseable HTTP before any application handling.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That Ferrum specifically generated it (no Ferrum body/header marker is present) or any gateway policy decision.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: fix the request format.
outcomes.notes: Exact hyper status/body per failure kind is library behaviour and must be lab-verified; not Ferrum-authored.

outcomes.condition: No complete request head delivered within FERRUM_HTTP_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 10) after accept/TLS (slowloris, idle H2 preface).

public_signal.transport: connection closed without an HTTP response (hard close)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server closed the connection before a request was accepted, consistent with a gateway header-read timeout.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Any HTTP status or backend involvement.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send the full request head promptly; check slow proxies.
outcomes.notes: Idle keep-alive after the first request is not bounded by this.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_FRONTEND_TLS_CLIENT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH (or _SOURCE) configured on the proxy frontend: rustls WebPkiClientVerifier built WITHOUT allow_unauthenticated, so a client certificate is mandatory at the handshake and verified against the client CA bundle (+ CRLs via FERRUM_TLS_CRL_FILE_PATH).

public_signal.transport: TLS handshake aborted with a rustls alert (typically certificate_required when none is sent under TLS 1.3; bad_certificate/unknown_ca/certificate_expired/certificate_revoked-style alerts for invalid certificates — exact alert is rustls behaviour)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The TLS handshake with the gateway endpoint failed; the observed alert is consistent with the server requiring or rejecting a client certificate.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That an HTTP 401/403 was received, or that the API credential is wrong.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: select a client certificate issued by the gateway's trusted client CA, with matching key and valid dates.
outcomes.notes: Frontend mTLS is all-or-nothing per listener (no optional mode on the plain proxy frontend; mesh listeners have Required/Optional/None, src/tls/mod.rs:1574). mtls_auth plugin then maps a verified cert to a consumer (HTTP 401 on no match — see plugin outcomes). FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY-style no_verify disables client auth entirely (testing).

outcomes.condition: ClientHello without SNI or with an SNI that no configured certificate claims.

public_signal.transport: handshake completes with the fallback certificate; client-side hostname verification then fails if the name does not match

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway presented its default certificate for this host name; a name-mismatch failure is on the client-to-gateway leg.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend certificate is wrong.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: use the published host name; operator: add a certificate for this name.
outcomes.notes: A name that IS claimed but has no certificate compatible with the client's signature schemes fails the handshake instead (multi_cert.rs:152-156).

outcomes.condition: Client offers ALPN protocols none of which is h2 or http/1.1 (e.g. h3-only over TCP, or a custom protocol).

public_signal.transport: rustls aborts with no_application_protocol alert (rustls default when ALPN is configured and there is no overlap)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The TLS handshake failed because the client and gateway share no application protocol.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Authentication failure.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: offer h2 and/or http/1.1 over TCP; use QUIC for h3.
outcomes.notes: rustls behaviour; lab-verify.

outcomes.condition: Frontend TLS handshake not completed within FERRUM_FRONTEND_TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 10).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway endpoint closed the connection before the TLS handshake completed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Certificate rejection (no alert evidence) or backend involvement.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check network path and client TLS stack.

outcomes.condition: Backend response fits the effective response ceiling but response_transformer JSON body rules would produce output larger than it (issue #4784).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Response body too large","limit":<retained response ceiling bytes>}
public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response replacing the backend response; gRPC/gRPC-Web: HTTP 200 grpc-status 8 grpc-message 'Response body too large'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to deliver this response because a gateway response transformation would exceed the gateway's response size ceiling; the backend did answer.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway is CPU/memory overloaded (despite the overload token) or that the origin body itself exceeded the ceiling.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator/API owner: adjust the response transformation rules or the route response ceiling.
outcomes.notes: Only X-Gateway-Error: overload case that is not a 503; the {"error","limit"} body shape distinguishes it from the overload 503.

outcomes.condition: A configured response body policy (validator, WAF, transformer, AI guard) cannot decode/inspect the backend's representation (unsupported/malformed content-encoding etc.); fail-closed.

public_signal.transport: HTTP complete response; gRPC 200 trailers-only grpc-status 13 same message

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge withheld the backend response because a gateway response policy could not inspect its encoding.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned 502.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: return an encoding the gateway supports (identity/gzip/etc.); operator: review response body policies.
outcomes.notes: X-Gateway-Error assumed backend_error because this rewrites the status on the backend-response builder path (connection_error=false, 502); not lab-verified. Reason recorded in metadata ferrum:representation_rejected.

outcomes.condition: A request body policy cannot inspect the request's Content-Encoding (malformed or unsupported coding).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because a gateway policy could not decode its Content-Encoding.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the JSON/schema content is invalid.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send an identity or supported encoding.

outcomes.condition: A mandatory replay response-redaction transform failed.

public_signal.x_gateway_error: only if status>=500 was already sent
public_signal.transport: HTTP/1.1: body ends without chunked terminator / short of Content-Length, connection closed; HTTP/2: stream reset (hyper sends RST_STREAM, INTERNAL_ERROR expected — library behaviour); HTTP/3: stream reset. No trailer or marker is synthesized for plain HTTP.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Response headers arrived but the response body did not complete; the transfer was cut by the gateway or upstream after the status was sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the response is complete or successful because the status was 2xx, that the gateway returned a 502, which cause (backend reset, idle timeout, size limit, credential expiry) applied, or that a non-idempotent request is safe to replay.
outcomes.remediation: Treat the result as incomplete; retry only idempotent requests; API owner/gateway operator: correlate gateway logs (body_error_class) for the cause.
outcomes.notes: Status and headers cannot be changed after commit; no X-Gateway-Error is added. error_class may be connection_closed / connection_reset / protocol_error (classify_body_error).

outcomes.condition: TCP (or TCP+TLS terminated) stream: backend DNS failure, connect failure, backend TLS failure, no healthy targets, circuit breaker open, backend max connections, stream plugin reject (ACL/throttle), authorization expired, client trust withdrawn, unsupported stream policy.

public_signal.transport: client connection closed without application data (after the frontend TLS handshake when the gateway terminates TLS)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway stream connection closed without delivering application data or a reason; L4 proxies cannot report the cause in-band.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific cause (backend down, policy reject, breaker, timeout) or that the backend received data.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: check the stream transaction log (error_class, disconnect_cause, disconnect_direction) for this connection.
outcomes.notes: Kinds are distinguishable only in StreamTransactionSummary (error_class, disconnect_cause, disconnect_direction). docs/tcp_udp_proxy.md:293: frontend TLS completes before backend connect, so a TLS client can see a successful handshake followed by close.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: No reply was observed within the wait window; UDP provides no delivery or rejection signal.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the datagram was delivered, rejected by policy, or that the gateway is down.
outcomes.remediation: Check gateway UDP session/drop counters and backend reachability.

public_signal.transport: frontend DTLS client-cert refusal (FERRUM_DTLS_CLIENT_CA_CERT_PATH): server discards its queued final flight; code comment (dtls/mod.rs:4241-4252) says dimpl close() during an in-progress handshake queues no alert, so a DTLS 1.2 client sees an incomplete handshake/retransmits; DTLS 1.3 peer is torn down after the server Finished

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The DTLS handshake with the gateway was refused or did not complete.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected application data.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check DTLS client certificate/trust.
outcomes.notes: Code comment and docs/frontend_tls.md:270-287 disagree on whether an alert is sent under DTLS 1.2 (doc: 'emits the refusal alert'; code comment: close() queues no alert during an in-progress handshake). Lab-verify. Backend DTLS origination failures are only visible as silence (StreamSetupKind::BackendDtlsHandshake).
